title: MultiMesh: indirect command buffer (StorageBuffer) leaks when the multimesh is freed or reallocated
body:
### Godot version

master (`34d06658a858`); the code is unchanged since the feature landed in #99455 (milestone 4.4).

### System information

Any Forward+ platform; observed on Windows 11 in a project that creates and frees indirect MultiMeshes at runtime.

### Issue description

`MeshStorage::_multimesh_allocate_data` (`servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/mesh_storage.cpp`) frees the instance `buffer` when reallocating, but overwrites the indirect **command buffer** with an empty RID without freeing it:

```cpp
multimesh->indirect = p_use_indirect;
multimesh->command_buffer = RID();
```

`_multimesh_free` funnels through `_multimesh_allocate_data(p_rid, 0, MULTIMESH_TRANSFORM_2D)`, so every indirect MultiMesh whose command buffer was allocated (any `multimesh_set_mesh` on a mesh with surfaces) orphans one RD StorageBuffer when freed. The same line also orphans the buffer on any mid-life reallocation. The only free site for `command_buffer` is the reallocation inside `_multimesh_set_mesh`.

At exit, `RenderingDevice::_free_rids` reports them:

```
WARNING: N RIDs of type "StorageBuffer" were leaked.
```

### Steps to reproduce

```gdscript
extends Node

func _ready() -> void:
	var mesh := QuadMesh.new()
	var mesh_rid := mesh.get_rid()
	for i in 50:
		var mm := RenderingServer.multimesh_create()
		RenderingServer.multimesh_allocate_data(mm, 4,
				RenderingServer.MULTIMESH_TRANSFORM_3D, false, false, true)
		RenderingServer.multimesh_set_mesh(mm, mesh_rid)
		RenderingServer.free(mm)
	get_tree().quit()
```

### What happens

Exit prints `WARNING: 50 RIDs of type "StorageBuffer" were leaked.` — one per freed indirect MultiMesh. Non-indirect MultiMeshes leak nothing.

### Suggested fix

Free at the overwrite, mirroring the guarded free `_multimesh_set_mesh` already performs on its reallocation path:

```cpp
if (multimesh->command_buffer.is_valid()) {
	RD::get_singleton()->free_rid(multimesh->command_buffer);
}
multimesh->command_buffer = RID();
```

This is safe with in-flight frames for the same reason the existing `_multimesh_set_mesh` free is: `RenderingDevice` defers storage-buffer disposal to frame-index recycling.
